title: Food and drink
cando: say what you like and want, order in a café and ask the price

about.text: This lesson is about food and drink. You say what you like. You order in a café.
goals: Say: I like tea. I don't like coffee.
Order: I'd like a tea, please.
Read a price list. Write a shopping list.

chapters.title: A cup of tea, please
chapters.text:
Carlos is in a café near work.
He orders tea.
I'd like a cup of tea, please.
The worker asks: Anything else?
Carlos is hungry. He wants a sandwich.
Then he asks: How much is it?

chapters.title: Like and want
chapters.text:
Like is about always.
I like tea. I don't like coffee.
Want is about now.
I'm thirsty. I want water now.
In a café, say I'd like.
I'd like a tea, please.
Say: I'm hungry. Not: I have hungry.

chapters.title: What I eat
chapters.text:
Next, you read a café price list.
Then Omar says what he eats.
Then you write a shopping list.

chapters.title: At the café
chapters.text:
Then you order in a café.
Ask for a drink and some food.
Ask: How much is it?
Then pay.

chapters.title: The book
chapters.text:
Last, you read a short story.
Read it once for the story.
Then read it again. Answer the questions.

warmup.prompt: You are in a café. What do you drink?
warmup.note: There is no wrong answer. In Britain, tea often has milk.

sound.title: eat and it
sound.explain: Eat has a long sound. It has a short sound. Make eat long. Make it short. Listen, then say each group.

sayIt.instructions: Say Carlos's lines. Record yourself. Then listen back. Is your voice clear?
lines: I'd like a cup of tea, please.
Egg, please. I don't like fish.

spot.instructions: Look at these sentences from the conversation.
examples: I'd like a cup of tea, please.
spot.question: Which sentence is about now? Which are about always? What word is before hungry?
spot.answer: I'd like is about now. Carlos wants tea now. I like, I don't like: always. I'm hungry: I am, not I have.

rules.title: Like, want, and I'm hungry
rule: Always: I like tea. I don't like coffee.
Now: I'm thirsty. I want water.
Café: I'd like a tea, please.
rules.mistake: Not: I like a tea, please. Say: I'd like a tea, please.

practice.why: Say: I don't like, with don't.

practice.q: I'm ___ . Can I have a sandwich?
practice.why: You want food. You are hungry.

practice.q: I'm ___ . Can I have some water?
practice.why: You want a drink. You are thirsty.
Say: I am hungry. Not: I have hungry.

yourTurn.prompt: What food and drink do you like? Write three lines.
yourTurn.model: I like tea with milk. I don't like coffee. I'm hungry. I'd like a sandwich.

text.title: What I eat
text.type: A price list and a short text
text.body:
THE CORNER CAFÉ
Drinks
Tea £2
Coffee £3
Juice £2
Water £1
Food
Egg sandwich £4
Fish and rice £7
Fruit £2

WHAT I EAT
by Omar
At home, I eat bread and eggs.
At work, I eat rice and fish.
I like fruit. I eat it every day.
I drink water and tea.
I don't like coffee.

gist.why: It has drinks, food and prices.
His title is What I eat.

detail.q: Tea and an egg sandwich: how much?
What does Omar eat at work?
detail.why: At work, I eat rice and fish.

detail.q: Which drink does Omar not like?
detail.why: He says: I don't like coffee.

items.meaning: Small, white food. You cook it in water.
It comes from a bird. You cook it.
It lives in water. You can eat it.
Sweet food, like apples and oranges.

card.title: At the café
card.situation: You are hungry and thirsty. You go to a café. You have £10.
card.goal: Order a drink and something to eat. Ask the price. Pay.

prepare.notes: Look at the price list. Choose a drink and some food. Write the price.

doIt.liveClass: Your teacher works in the café. Order a drink and some food. Ask the price and pay. Then change roles.
doIt.wehel: You work in a café. I want a drink and some food. Ask me: What would you like? Tell me the price. Use very simple English.

reading.before: Look at the title. Look at the first picture. What food can you see?

quiz.q: I'd ___ a cup of tea, please.
Tea with milk? Yes, please. No ___ .

quiz.why: You drink juice. You eat bread and rice.

quiz.q: Which has the long sound of eat?
quiz.why: Tea and eat: the same long sound.

quiz.q: Six pounds. How do you write it?

quiz.why: The colour comes first: a black bag.

liveClass: Day 1: practise the café conversation in pairs. Then a like and don't like round: each learner says one food they like and one they don't.
Day 2: the task. You are the café worker, with the Corner Café price list. Each learner orders a drink and something to eat, asks the price and pays.
Day 3: talk about the book. Then learners read their shopping lists aloud, and the others say I like it or I don't like it.
